taxonomic_note: POWO accepts Acmella repens (Walter) Rich. The older regional name Acmella oppositifolia var. repens and historic Spilanthes americana concepts refer to this taxon in some floras; do not create a second card from those names without concept checking.
look_here_first: Follow a trailing stem to a node: opposite petiolate, toothed leaves and stems that can root at the nodes. Then inspect a long-stalked solitary head: the disk becomes a conspicuous elongated conical receptacle with chaffy paleae as fruits mature. Confirm with mature compressed dark cypselae; ray color alone is weak.

project_inclusion.learner_admission_basis: Calvin-approved Master Plant Pool row 17 (My iNaturalist Flora and Personal List); existing taxonomy review 2026-10-09
project_inclusion.range_basis: POWO accepts native Texas distribution at state level, but three target-zone county proofs have not been established. No target-zone native PASS.

morphology_keys.habit: Creeping to sprawling perennial herb in moist or disturbed ground; lower stem nodes may root.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite petiolate leaves, usually lanceolate to ovate, serrate; upper leaves may vary in position.
morphology_keys.heads: Solitary pedunculate composite heads with small yellowish rays and disk; receptacle elongates to a cone with persistent chaffy paleae in fruit.
morphology_keys.fruits: Compressed dark cypselae about 1–2.5 mm; pappus generally absent. Look for fruiting cone and paleae.
best_field_traits: opposite toothed petiolate leaves at rooting nodes
small dark cypselae usually without pappus

comparisons.key_distinctions: Eclipta prostrata also has opposite leaves and wet-ground habit, but usually has small white rays and different fruit/head architecture. Synedrella nodiflora bears small axillary or terminal heads and a more erect habit; compare ray/cypsela morphology. Sphagneticola trilobata often has 3-lobed leaves and much larger showy rays. Confirm the elongated chaffy receptacle and fruit, not just leaf arrangement.

show elongated conical receptacle and chaffy paleae
show small rays and conical disk
